title: Intersectionality: The Failure of Single-Axis Bias Auditing
text:
A critical ethical blind spot in bias auditing is the assumption that fairness can be maintained by testing marginalized identity groups in isolation. Standard diagnostic tools often measure disparate impact across single axes (e.g., gender or race) independently, failing to detect differential harm that arises at the intersections of multiple oppressed identities.

When an algorithm's performance degradation affects a population only characterized by the overlap of traits—such as Black women or low-income Indigenous individuals—these specialized vulnerabilities can be entirely invisible. Responsible deployment mandates moving beyond siloed metrics toward intersectional fairness analysis, recognizing that moral harms are compounded, not merely additive.

Failure to implement this multidimensional auditing approach results in a dangerous gap between technical compliance and actual equitable function, risking the systemic exclusion of those whose experiences fall outside conventional linear models of disparity.
